# An exact obstruction to the free-mixture selector, with simplex endpoints

This is an auxiliary counterexample, NOT a counterexample to OC. It proves
that even checking every endpoint point and every point of the proposed
free-mixture selector need not find an OC point. All three fibers are
positive five-dimensional simplices, with strictly nonheavy volumes.

## 1. A simplex midpoint body in a thin wedge

Let d=5 and let B be the standard simplex in R^5. Its centroid is
g=(1/6,...,1/6), and its volume is 1/120. Throughout the calculations
below volumes are divided by |B|. Put

    R=9/2,
    r=497/3000=1/6-1/1000,
    ell=11/12-Rr,
    T=1-r-ell=3979/6000.

Let D be the five-dimensional simplex with apex and five base vertices

    p=(0,11/12,0,0,0),
    b_0=(r,ell,0,0,0),
    b_i=b_0+T e_i,       i=2,3,4,5.

All vertices lie in B. Every vertex, and hence every point of D, satisfies

    x_1<=r<1/6,
    R x_1+x_2>=11/12=(R+1)/6.                         (1)

The base has four-dimensional volume T^4/24 and its distance from p
is r. Thus D has relative volume

    m=|D|/|B|=r T^4
      =124581095445185057/3888000000000000000.

Exact rational comparisons are

 m-1/32 =3081095445185057/3888000000000000000 >0,
 (11/20)^5-m
       =71095869554814943/3888000000000000000 >0.        (2)

## 2. The three actual integer fibers

Put

    q=m^(-1/5), A=(2-q)D, C=qD,
    a=|A|/|B|=(2m^(1/5)-1)^5.

By (2), 0<2-q, q<2, and

    0<a<(1/10)^5=10^(-5).                              (3)

Also |C|/|B|=1. The midpoint identity (A+C)/2=D follows from convexity
and the two homothety factors summing to two. In particular it is
contained in B. Let the ambient convex body be

    mathcal C=conv( ({-1}xA) union ({0}xB) union ({1}xC) ).

Its integer fibers are exactly A,B,C. Its middle hull adds only D,
already contained in B, while the endpoints are extreme integer indices.
It is a full-dimensional convex body, and its integer projection is
{-1,0,1}. The relative fiber volumes are a,1,1, with a>0, so every
fiber has volume strictly below half the total 2+a.

## 3. The entire proposed middle candidate set lies in a fixed cone hull

For any sigma<=1_C dx of mass |A|, its centroid lies in C=qD. Hence

    (g_A+g_sigma)/2 belongs to D.

Indeed g_A=(2-q)g_D, and writing g_sigma=q w with w in D expresses
this midpoint as the convex combination
(1-q/2)g_D+(q/2)w. Therefore the entire free-mixture selector satisfies

    Z=conv({g} union {(g_A+g_sigma)/2: sigma<=1_C dx,
                                      sigma(C)=|A|})
       subset conv({g} union D).                       (4)

This inclusion covers all fractional submeasure selectors and all
mixture coefficients, not only uniform subset selectors.

## 4. Two bad ambient caps cover the larger hull in (4)

Set

    alpha=2/25, beta=17/50,
    h_1=1/6-alpha a, h_2=1/6+beta a,

and define closed ambient halfspaces

    H_1={ (z,x): x_1+(1-q)r z>=h_1 },
    H_2={ (z,x): x_2-2z>=h_2 }.                        (5)

The first cap excludes both endpoint fibers. On A at z=-1 its maximum
margin expression is (2-q)r-(1-q)r=r; on C at z=1 it is qr+(1-q)r=r.
But h_1>r by (3), since alpha a<10^(-3). Thus only its B cap contributes.

The second cap contains the entire A fiber: every point there has
x_2+2>=2>h_2. It excludes C, since C subset qB and q<2 give x_2-2<0<h_2.
The threshold inequalities used here follow directly from (3).

For any y=(1-t)g+t x with x in D and 0<=t<=1, either y_1>=h_1 and
(0,y) belongs to H_1, or

    t(1/6-x_1)>alpha a.

In the latter case the wedge inequality (1) gives

 y_2-1/6=t(x_2-1/6)
       >=R t(1/6-x_1)>R alpha a=(9/25)a>beta a.

Thus (0,y) belongs to H_2. Consequently H_1 union H_2 covers the
ENTIRE larger hull conv({g} union D), and hence all of Z. The equality
case y_1=h_1 is included by the closedness of H_1.

## 5. Both cap masses are strictly below OC

Let gamma=gamma_5=(5/6)^5=3125/7776. In relative volume units,

    mu(H_1)/|B|=(1-h_1)^5=gamma[1+(12/125)a]^5,
    mu(H_2)/|B|=(1-h_2)^5+a=gamma[1-(51/125)a]^5+a.

The OC target in these units is gamma(2+a)/2=gamma(1+a/2).
We use only the weaker bound 0<a<=1/100, which follows from (3).

For the first cap the mean-value inequality gives

 ([1+(12/125)a]^5-1)/a
    <=(12/25)[1+(12/125)(1/100)]^4
     =1148810043113472/2384185791015625 <1/2.           (6)

For the second, the polynomial inequality
(1-t)^5<=1-5t+10t^2 holds for 0<=t<=1, since the omitted part is
-t^3(10-5t+t^2)<=0. Its linear margin below the target is

    gamma(1/2+51/25)-1=323/15552>0.

The quadratic remainder per a is at most

    gamma*10*(51/125)^2*(1/100)<323/15552.               (7)

Thus the second cap is also strictly below gamma(1+a/2). Equations
(6)-(7) are exact rational inequalities, independently checked in the
companion verifier. Therefore EVERY point of Z has original mixed depth
strictly below gamma_5/2.

## 6. Every endpoint point also fails the OC target

Both A and C are simplices. A d-simplex of volume V has maximal ordinary
halfspace depth exactly gamma_d V. For the upper bound, every point has
a barycentric coordinate at least 1/(d+1); the vertex cap through it,
parallel to the opposite facet, has volume at most gamma_d V. At the
centroid equality follows from ordinary Grunbaum. At an extreme integer
fiber, any such own-fiber cap can be extended with a sufficiently large
integer tilt to exclude all other fibers. Thus every endpoint point has
absolute mixed depth at most respectively gamma a or gamma, in the
same relative units.

Both quantities are strictly below gamma(1+a/2): for C this uses a>0,
and for A it follows from a<1. Hence neither endpoint, including its
ordinary deepest point, repairs this example.

The example is an exact obstruction to the selector set Z together with
all endpoint points. It does not bound the depth of middle-fiber points
outside conv({g} union D), and makes no assertion against OC itself.
